name: E2B

facts.value: E2B Cloud
facts.notes: Vendor-operated Firecracker Linux sandboxes on Google Cloud; Hobby, Pro and Enterprise. US default on all plans; EU and APAC require Pro or above and support enablement. Projects/API keys/templates/sandboxes/volumes are region-scoped; no cross-region template copy, build separately. API key required; exhausted credits block usage until payment method added. Public-cloud terms do not automatically apply to Embed or negotiated BYOC.

facts.value: E2B Embed and open-source E2B runtime
facts.notes: Single-node control plane/runtime/storage via Compose, AWS/GCP/Azure Terraform or Kubernetes; no E2B account/license key. Live preflight supports x86_64 and aarch64 with KVM, 4 KiB host pages, kernel >=6.8 x86 or >=6.10 arm, glibc >=2.34, cgroup v2/TUN/NBD/host tools and default 20 GiB host free disk. Mac use is nested Linux VM on M3+/macOS15+, not native macOS guest. Marketing still names x86-64 only; pinned release/artifact availability matters. Plain HTTP/header routing, not managed public HTTPS; operator firewalls internal ports including unauthenticated5008. Launcher shutdown ends sandboxes; local storage is not a node-failure guarantee. BYOP unsupported by open runtime; Secrets launch does not establish Embed parity.

facts.value: Enterprise managed deployment in the customer AWS, GCP, or Azure account and VPC
facts.notes: Contact sales/onboarding required. E2B provisions and monitors the cluster; templates, snapshots, logs and sensitive sandbox/build traffic stay in the customer VPC, while anonymized system metrics go to E2B Cloud. This is not customer-operated self-hosting. A separate private-cloud offering with the whole control plane inside the customer boundary remains in development.

facts.value: Python and JavaScript/TypeScript
facts.notes: Packages are named e2b. A CLI is documented separately.

facts.value: Go (third-party community SDKs; not vendor-maintained)
facts.notes: Public third-party Go repositories provide E2B sandbox lifecycle, command, and filesystem SDKs, including a package with documented create/connect, commands, files, PTY, volumes, and templates. This establishes the existence of community Go clients, not E2B endorsement, official support, quality, or current compatibility. E2B official SDK inventory remains Python and JavaScript/TypeScript.

facts.value: Available
facts.notes: Docs index lists sandbox, template, snapshot, and volume HTTP endpoints, including v2 routes.

facts.value: Available
facts.notes: CLI docs cover auth, create, exec, fork, snapshots, and shutdown.

facts.value: Linux guest; Code Interpreter supports Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, R, Java, and Bash
facts.notes: Code Interpreter's language list is not the contents of every base template. Default base includes Python 3 and Node.js; other runtimes can be installed in a compatible custom template. SDK languages do not limit guest execution.

facts.value: Firecracker microVM with its own kernel
facts.notes: Homepage summary: hardware-isolated microVM rather than a shared-kernel container.

facts.value: Linux
facts.notes: Default base is Debian-based; compatible template images include Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/RHEL family, Arch and Alpine, plus the prepared e2bdev/nixos image. Images without identifiable /etc/os-release or required packages fail provisioning. Template kernel is LTS Linux 6.1, fixed at build time; rebuild to change it. Desktop is an Ubuntu/VNC template, not a different hosted OS guarantee.

facts.value: 1 to 8 vCPUs on the published self-serve range; Pro and Enterprise can be higher
facts.notes: Pricing page says the default sandbox has 2 vCPUs. Billing FAQ instead says to start with 2 vCPU. Both agree on 2 vCPU as a default CPU figure.

facts.value: Pricing 1-8 GiB; template API minimum 128 MiB; base documented 512 MiB
facts.notes: Different defaults remain: pricing says 4 GiB, base/billing/cost FAQ 512 MiB; build-limits FAQ says rebuild without resource parameters defaults to 1024 MiB. Base instance vs custom build scope is distinct, not a universal default. API memoryMB described in MiB with schema minimum128; SDK BuildOptions comment calls it MB, retain unit conflict. Hobby max8 GiB, Pro8+ via support, EnterpriseCustom; schema acceptance is not operational guarantee for every plan/image. Do not normalize MB/MiB/GiB or assert1GiB universal minimum.

facts.value: Included free disk headroom: Hobby 10 GiB; Pro 20+ GiB; Enterprise custom
facts.notes: Build-limits FAQ explicitly says free space above image contents, not maximum template size; total filesystem can be larger. Plan applied at build time; higher Pro needs support and rebuild. Separate uncompressed base-image cap is team-specific, reported in build error, raise via support; post-unpack copy/run data not part of image-size cap. API/SDK minFreeDiskMb in MiB requests best-effort free growth, omit uses team default, zero no growth, never shrinks. Pricing/billing shorthand calls10/20GiB storage/disk; no pooled account allowance or all volume/snapshot meters implied free.

facts.value: No GPU sandboxes
facts.notes: GPU FAQ and current pricing explicitly say CPU-only, with no GPU option in SDKs, CLI, API or template definition; BYOC does not change this. Remote model inference is not an attached GPU.

facts.value: Reusable templates from compatible linux/amd64 images, Dockerfiles and private registries
facts.notes: V2 SDK >=2.3, general/GCP Artifact Registry/AWS ECR credentials. Migration docs explicitly require linux/amd64 images for fromImage; not proof of same guest architecture on arm64 Embed. Parser no multi-stage Dockerfiles, EXPOSE/VOLUME skipped, unsuitable OS/minimal images fail; prebuilt multi-stage Docker image can be imported after external build. Prepared e2bdev/nixos supported. Base-image uncompressed size cap team-specific/error/support, separate from10/20GiB free headroom; exact cap unknown. Whole build/single command1h; readiness/copy10min, layer upload30min, queued40min; only one build/name+tag, new supersedes old.20 concurrent Hobby/Pro, EnterpriseCustom, higher resources require rebuild with explicit parameters. Tags mutable; pin build ID for exact artifact; no cross-region copy, build each region.

facts.value: Template build steps and runtime package installation
facts.notes: pip/npm and sudo apt examples. Runtime changes stay in that instance unless explicitly paused/snapshotted or exported; a fresh base-template instance does not inherit them. Package manager must exist and network policy must permit downloads. Default Debian guidance is not a restriction to Debian-only custom templates.

facts.value: Guest root selection and sudo are documented
facts.notes: Default template user is user, /home/user. PTY examples explicitly select user='root'; Docker examples run sudo during build and runtime; package quickstart uses sudo apt. Guest privileges, not host root, and custom templates can choose another default user.

facts.value: Docker and Docker Compose inside a prepared guest template
facts.notes: Ubuntu 24.04 example installs Docker, validates hello-world and runs sudo docker in the sandbox. Vendor recommends at least 2 CPUs and 2 GB RAM; example uses cpuCount 2 and memoryMB 2048. Lower RAM can OOM. This is guest Docker, not host/container isolation or Docker preinstalled in every base template.

facts.value: Background commands survive SDK disconnection while the sandbox runs
facts.notes: commands.run background=true returns immediately; default command timeout is 60 seconds and kills the process even in background. Set command timeout 0 to disable it and separately extend sandbox TTL. Persist sandbox ID/pid to reconnect; redirect output to a file because streams are not replayed and can stall after connection loss. Full pause restores processes, filesystem-only/reboot does not; external connections drop. SDK/CLI fork count is 1-20 from SDK 2.52.0/CLI 2.21.0 (API schema still max 100); forks default to 15-second TTL and consume concurrency. Hobby/Pro create rate 1/5 per second, separate from 20/100 default running slots.

facts.value: SDK filesystem upload/download and template file seeding
facts.notes: Read/write files; multi-file upload available, but no simple whole-directory upload/download and multiple downloads are separate calls. Export must precede destructive kill; export/import is not process-memory recovery.

facts.value: Explicit pause keeps root files; saved snapshots or private-beta volumes enable replacement recovery
facts.notes: Paused state retained indefinitely until kill; default timeout kills and cannot resume. Full pause preserves memory too; filesystem-only pause reboots. Rebooting a memory-inclusive snapshot loses unflushed writes: flush/sync first. Saved snapshot can spawn new instances beyond source lifetime; volume data independently survives sandbox shutdown but requires private-beta access, fixed mounts at create, and is not a root-disk guarantee. Unexpected host/failure recovery guarantees not established.

facts.value: Private-beta persistent volumes; separately configured S3/GCS/R2 bucket mounts
facts.notes: Volume access requires support; managed volumes US/EU only, not APAC. Independent data survives sandbox shutdown and mounts can be shared; set at create and cannot replace through resume/connect/fork. No volume snapshots, server-side copies or read-only mounts; locking can hang, small-file operations have network overhead, permission bits are not enforced between guest users, and deleting a mounted volume can prevent resume. Buckets require FUSE/custom template, external account/credentials and external storage terms, not a native-volume equivalence.

facts.value: Explicit pause/connect and opt-in timeout pause/auto-resume
facts.notes: Full pause saves root filesystem and memory indefinitely; kill is terminal and timeout defaults to kill. Paused sandboxes not billed for compute or counted in running concurrency. Auto-resume requires a memory snapshot; after wake TTL is at least 5 minutes or original longer value, not reset by ordinary activity. Pause can be refused while previous snapshot persists (503 behavior rolling out; earlier regions may return 500); sandbox keeps running under the documented new behavior, so wait for success before assuming suspension/billing stop. Auto-pause snapshot backlog can fall back to disk-only after about two minutes. Network clients must reconnect.

facts.value: Full pause and memory snapshots restore processes; not every recovery transition
facts.notes: Default full pause saves RAM/processes; filesystem-only pause and onResume='reboot' discard memory and reboot. Reboot drops unflushed writes. During region-by-region pause-refusal rollout, auto-pause can fall back to filesystem-only after roughly two minutes of snapshot backlog, losing memory. External network connections always disconnect. Self-hosted control planes need compatible version/feature enablement for reboot; older versions can ignore it. Not an unconditional host-failure recovery guarantee.

facts.value: Persistent root-filesystem checkpoints with default memory restore spawn new sandboxes
facts.notes: envd>=0.5.0, rebuild older templates. Source briefly pauses then continues same ID; WebSocket/PTY/command streams drop. Snapshot template/tag outlives source; spawn via ID, delete explicitly. REST create-snapshot accepts memory=false for disk-only new-instance cold boot; JS main SDK createSnapshot exposes name but does not forward a memory option, unlike keepMemory on pause. No uniform standalone retention/quota/rate/price published; template count unrestricted but100-item list pages are pagination, not total quota. Private-beta volumes no snapshots; external mounts not documented backed up by root checkpoint. Snapshot name can update existing template build/tag, not immutable historical-name guarantee.

facts.value: SDK/CLI 1-20 forks per call; REST schema maximum 100
facts.notes: October 5 changelog: SDK >=2.52.0 and CLI >=2.21.0 reject counts outside 1-20; marketing and REST schema still say 100. Preserve interface distinction; no universal 100-copy SDK claim. Capture once; independent IDs/state/timeouts, original keeps ID/expiry and uses a concurrency slot. Fork TTL defaults to 15 seconds; count also below team's concurrent limit. Write-heavy source pauses longer and streams disconnect; individual copies can fail independently. Saved snapshots are reusable checkpoints, fork call capture is used for that call. No numeric reset/fork latency established.

facts.value: Public outbound internet on by default; opt-in deny-all
facts.notes: allowInternetAccess=false is documented as denyOut 0.0.0.0/0. Platform separately blocks private/link-local address ranges outside guest; platform control-channel return traffic is an exception. Domain allowlists automatically allow DNS to 8.8.8.8. Disabling outbound does not secure public ingress; configure allowPublicTraffic separately.

facts.value: IP/CIDR allow/deny; domain allowlists only with default deny
facts.notes: No domain deny lists. Domain inspection HTTP Host:80/TLS SNI:443 only; other ports CIDR, no QUIC domain filter. Domain use auto-allows DNS8.8.8.8; allow overrides deny. Shared CDN/storage endpoint may allow other destinations, not blanket isolation. Blocked socket may look open; verify application response. updateNetwork replaces/omitted fields clear, not merge. Public ingress separate; HTTPS transforms public beta. BYOP private beta Cloud/BYOC: TCP after filtering, fails closed on proxy failure; UDP/DNS bypass. API-only TLS hop to proxy, current SDK only forwards address/user/password, discarding TLS option. Open runtime rejects BYOP despite broad Embed marketing; guest tunnel bypassable. No static managed E2B egress IP any plan; own proxy can provide one.

facts.value: Managed-cloud HTTPS proxy to services inside sandbox; not general raw TCP ingress
facts.notes: getHost(port) produces https://{port}-{sandboxId}.e2b.app. Service must listen on reachable interface (docs use 0.0.0.0); proxy terminates external TLS and normally forwards HTTP. httpsPorts at creation re-encrypts to guest TLS without certificate verification, not TLS passthrough. Public by default; allowPublicTraffic=false requires e2b-traffic-access-token header (403 without). Pause disconnects clients; opt-in memory auto-resume can wake service, kill ends it. SSH requires installed OpenSSH plus WebSocket proxy, not raw port-22 forwarding. Self-hosted Embed is plain HTTP/header routing and does not supply managed HTTPS hostnames; BYOC private load balancer is deployment-specific.

facts.value: Managed-cloud public HTTPS sandbox service URLs via getHost(port)
facts.notes: Anyone knowing URL can reach listening service by default, including Code Interpreter port 49999 if present. Restrict public traffic to require per-sandbox token header. HTTPS terminates at proxy; guest HTTP default, optional httpsPorts re-encryption with unverified guest certificate. Running lifetime or enabled memory auto-resume only; clients reconnect after pause. Not raw TCP/SSH; self-hosted Embed needs header routing and customer TLS setup instead of these public hostnames. Custom-domain guide uses customer-operated GCP/Caddy proxy and Cloudflare DNS, not a native managed custom-domain promise.

facts.value: Enterprise BYOC internal load balancer and VPC connectivity
facts.notes: Contact sales and configure internal load balancer/VPC peering; Azure uses internal load balancer plus customer Private Link service/private endpoint. E2B-operated deployment, not a generally available shared-cloud sandbox-to-sandbox private mesh. Shared-cloud docs block private/link-local outbound ranges outside guest; proxy tunneling alone is not private network eligibility. Exact BYOC egress-policy interactions require deployment-specific confirmation.

facts.value: Hobby 20; Pro 100, Pro+ 600, Pro++ 1,100; Enterprise 1,100+ or custom
facts.notes: Running sandboxes only; paused do not count. Billing now says each $500/month add-on adds 500 slots, up to 1,100 on Pro; pricing prints total plan/add-on fees $650 and $1,150. Enterprise custom capacity is negotiated, not guaranteed. Separate creation rates 1/sec Hobby, 5/sec Pro; listed GET rates 10/20 per project/endpoint, Enterprise custom. Fork source consumes a slot and SDK/CLI max per call is 20.

facts.value: Hobby 1 hour continuous; Pro 24 hours continuous; Enterprise custom
facts.notes: Billing docs say this is continuous runtime without a pause, not a cap on how long a sandbox can exist. Pausing resets it. Paused retention is unlimited.

facts.value: Configurable running TTL, default 5 minutes; not an established idle detector
facts.notes: Default timeout action is destructive kill; opt into onTimeout='pause'. Commands/files/HTTP activity do not reset running TTL. setTimeout resets from now; connect only extends to later of current expiry and now+timeout (default 300 seconds). Auto-resume gets at least 5 minutes or original longer timeout, not a 5-minute billing minimum. Billing FAQ calls this inactivity/auto-pause, but lifecycle docs explicitly describe fixed TTL. Continuous runtime caps are Hobby 1 hour/Pro 24 hours; pause/resume resets that window.

facts.value: Listed GET endpoints: Hobby 10 and Pro 20 requests/second per project per endpoint; Enterprise custom
facts.notes: Includes list sandboxes/metrics/snapshots/templates/API keys/volumes/secrets; path IDs and API keys share the endpoint allowance; pagination requests count. Not a universal rate for all methods. Creation separately 1/sec Hobby, 5/sec Pro, Enterprise custom. 429 returns Retry-After; SDK >=2.49.1 retries these; SDK 2.52.0 also handles documented 502/503 responses with retry policy. Exact fork/reset write rates not published in the reviewed table.

facts.value: Cloud Google regions: US us-west1; EU europe-west1; APAC asia-southeast1
facts.notes: US default/all plans; EU and APAC Pro+ and support-enabled domain/project. State/API keys/templates/volumes region-scoped; no region option or cross-region template copy, build once per region. Docs list current Google placements but warn they may span/change regions, not fixed E2B CIDRs/static egress IP on any plan. Private-beta volumes only US/EU, not APAC. Region multipliers not published; Enterprise negotiates pricing/regions and BYOC region/customer quotas during onboarding. Unified console does not unify regional state.

facts.value: Supported
facts.notes: Command docs include streaming output.

facts.value: Sandbox logs API and metrics; Enterprise OTel export
facts.notes: GET /v2/sandboxes/{id}/logs supports cursor/limit/direction/level/search; max1000 per request is not retention. Managed OTel Enterprise/onboarding, best effort/drop possible. Lifecycle-events API7-day retention is separate from general sandbox output-log retention, which remains unestablished. Embed ClickHouse logs7days and configured collector separate. Enterprise SLA negotiated, not default log durability.

facts.value: Interactive PTY; SSH via prepared WebSocket proxy template
facts.notes: PTY bidirectional streaming and reconnect; default PTY timeout 60 seconds, disable with timeout 0 for longer sessions subject to sandbox TTL. SSH requires OpenSSH/websocat and wss proxy; not direct public TCP/22. Stream keepalives do not guarantee uninterrupted connections; pause/snapshot drops clients.

facts.value: Managed-cloud GA project-scoped write-only Secrets injected at egress HTTPS proxy; BYOC coming soon
facts.notes: October7,2026 launch explicitly GA, superseding Sept14 private-beta changelog; BYOC coming soon despite Enterprise table saying Yes. Embed parity not established. HTTPS transform itself public beta; no plainHTTP/arbitrary guest-env injection (direct in-guest delivery planned). Secret.fill formats placeholder locally; actual value injected outside guest. OpenAPI transform prose says client-side resolution, conflicting with SDK placeholder code and live guide/launch; no claimed client decryption. Destination may echo value. Missing/deleted/unavailable secret omits header but forwards traffic, including removal of conflicting guest header; scope destinations narrowly. Limits page100/project (API409 reports effective cap, example50),64KiB/value,32 names/host,256KiB/request; fixed10 domains/sandbox,1rule/domain,20headers/rule,2048char/value. Broad transform wildcard can expose credentials across matching hosts.

facts.value: API keys, sandbox traffic tokens and private-beta workload identity
facts.notes: API key authenticates SDK/CLI. Public URLs anonymous by default; allowPublicTraffic=false requires e2b-traffic-access-token. Workload identity private beta via support: up to 5 JWT-SVID tokens per sandbox, audience/project scoped, injected outside sandbox; external service verification/exchange required. Exchanged AWS credentials can outlive sandbox/token. These are distinct mechanisms, not a verified broad IAM/RBAC matrix or automatic ingress security.

facts.value: Many coding agents and desktop computer use
facts.notes: Docs index lists Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain, and an Ubuntu desktop for computer use, among others.

facts.value: Apache-2.0 for E2B runtime/Embed; official inventory also names SDKs and CLI
facts.notes: Runtime LICENSE and Embed README verified directly; hosted service has separate terms. Open-source client license is not the basis for self-hosted support; runtime/control-plane deployment is documented separately.

network_isolation.note: Opt-in outbound deny-all via allowInternetAccess=false/denyOut 0.0.0.0/0; not default isolation of public ingress. Domain policies add DNS exception; shared endpoints weaken destination isolation. Public URL access needs separate traffic-token policy. Embed requires operator firewall/TLS configuration.

egress_allowlist.note: IP/CIDR allow/deny; domains only allowed with default deny, not domain deny lists. HTTP Host:80 and TLS SNI:443 only; other ports CIDR, no QUIC domain filter. Automatic DNS 8.8.8.8 exception, allow beats deny, shared CDN/storage destinations can remain reachable. Network updates replace rules.

inbound_ports_or_preview_urls.note: Managed-cloud HTTPS service proxy via getHost(port), public by default or traffic-token restricted. TLS terminates at proxy; guest HTTP default, optional httpsPorts re-encryption without guest-cert verification. Pause disconnects clients; memory auto-resume optional. Not raw TCP/SSH. Embed is plain HTTP/header routing and needs customer TLS setup.

private_networking.note: Enterprise BYOC internal load balancer/VPC peering or Azure Private Link after onboarding; not an established generally available shared-cloud sandbox private mesh. Confirm BYOC egress-policy interactions for deployment.

snapshots.note: Root checkpoint envd>=0.5.0; source briefly pauses/streams drop then continues; spawn replacement beyond source lifetime. REST memory=false saves files/cold boots; JS main createSnapshot exposes name, not memory toggle. List100/page is not total quota; named snapshot/tag can update existing build. Retention/quota/prices unresolved; no volume/external backup guarantee.

memory_snapshot_or_live_resume.note: Full pause/snapshot restores RAM/processes; filesystem-only/reboot does not, and reboot loses unflushed writes. Snapshot-backlog auto-pause can fall back to disk-only after about two minutes during regional rollout. External clients always disconnect; no unconditional failure-recovery guarantee.

pause_resume.note: Explicit pause/connect; opt-in timeout pause and memory auto-resume. Timeout defaults to kill; ordinary activity does not reset TTL. Paused state retained indefinitely, no compute/concurrency charge. Pause refusal/backlog rollout may require retry or disk-only fallback; verify success before assuming paused.

cloning_forking.note: SDK >=2.52.0/CLI >=2.21.0 allow 1-20 forks per call; REST schema and marketing still max 100. Source retained; independent copies use running slots and default to 15-second TTL. Source pause depends on disk changes; streams drop and copies can fail independently.

persistent_filesystem.note: Explicit pause keeps root files indefinitely; default timeout/kill destroys resumability. Saved snapshots restore replacement files; independent volumes require private-beta access and fixed mounts. Reboot from memory-inclusive snapshot loses unflushed writes. No unexpected-node-failure durability guarantee established.

volumes.note: Support-gated private beta, US/EU managed cloud only. Independent shared data survives sandbox shutdown; mounts fixed at create. No volume snapshots/read-only mounts/server-side copies; locking can hang, permissions not enforced between users, deleting mounted volume can break resume. External FUSE buckets have separate credentials/terms.

custom_images.note: Documented linux/amd64 imported images/private credentials/v2 templates; parser no multistage, EXPOSE/VOLUME skipped, unsuitable OS/images fail; prepared NixOS supported. External prebuilt multistage image import distinct. Team-specific image cap versus10/20GiB free headroom. Build/command1h,ready/copy10min,upload30min,queued40min;20 concurrent Hobby/Pro. Tags mutable/pin build,build per region; arm64 Embed guest-image parity unresolved.

docker_in_sandbox.note: Prepared Ubuntu template installs/runs Docker and Compose in guest, not default base. Vendor recommends at least 2 CPUs and 2 GB RAM; example memoryMB 2048. Lower RAM may OOM.

root_sudo.note: Default user is user; PTY explicitly supports user root and Docker/package examples run sudo at build and runtime. Guest privileges, not host root; custom template user may differ.

gpu.note: The GPU FAQ says E2B sandboxes are CPU-only and BYOC does not add a GPU option.

self_hosted.note: Runtime/Embed Apache2 Linux Compose/AWS/GCP/Azure Terraform/Kubernetes. Live preflight x86_64/aarch64 KVM,4KiB pages,kernel>=6.8/6.10 respectively,glibc>=2.34,cgroupv2/TUN/NBD/tools/default20GiB host free. Marketing x86-only narrower. PlainHTTP/customer firewall/TLS and pinned compatible artifacts required; no hosted durability promise, BYOP unsupported.

byoc.note: Enterprise sales-gated AWS/GCP/Azure customer-VPC deployment operated by E2B; anonymized metrics go to E2B Cloud. Not self-hosting. Whole-platform private cloud remains in development.

open_source.note: Runtime LICENSE and Embed README state Apache-2.0; official inventory also names SDK/CLI. Hosted service terms separate.

background_processes.note: background option survives SDK disconnect; default command timeout 60 seconds kills process. Set 0 and extend sandbox TTL for long jobs; persist ID/pid and redirect logs. Full-memory pause restores processes, disk-only/reboot does not.

terminal_pty.note: Bidirectional PTY with disconnect/reconnect; default session timeout 60 seconds, 0 disables it, still subject to sandbox TTL. Keepalive does not guarantee uninterrupted stream; snapshots/pause disconnect clients.

command_streaming.note: commands.run streams stdout/stderr callbacks; SDK keepalive every 50 seconds, reconnect required after connection loss/pause/snapshot. Not replayed durable background log storage.

secrets_management.note: Managed Cloud Secrets GA per Oct7 launch; BYOC coming soon despite Enterprise tableYes, Embed parity unestablished. Project write-only placeholder proxy-injected HTTPS, not plainHTTP/guest env; in-guest delivery planned. Destination may echo; unresolved header omitted but traffic forwarded. Transforms public beta/broad wildcards unsafe. OpenAPI client-side-resolution prose conflicts with SDK placeholder/live guide.

python_sdk.note: Sandbox examples and the docs index include the Python SDK.

typescript_sdk.note: Sandbox examples and the docs index include the JavaScript/TypeScript SDK.

go_sdk.note: A public third-party Go SDK provides E2B sandbox lifecycle, commands, files, PTY, volumes, and templates. It is not E2B-maintained or endorsed; official E2B documentation lists Python and JavaScript/TypeScript clients. Current compatibility, maintenance, quality, and vendor support are unverified, so Go client availability is partial rather than a fully supported official SDK claim.

cli.note: The CLI docs cover auth, create, exec, fork, snapshots, and shutdown.

mcp_or_agent_integrations.note: The docs index documents an MCP gateway and agent guides including Claude, Codex, and Cursor.

max_vcpu.note: Hobby prints a maximum of 8 vCPUs. Pro prints 8+ and Enterprise is Custom, so no single numeric maximum is published.

max_memory_gib.note: Hobby prints 8 GiB. Pro prints 8+ GiB and Enterprise is Custom, so no single numeric maximum is published.

max_session_duration_seconds.note: No product-wide numeric maximum: Pro continuous runtime is 24 hours (86400 seconds), Hobby 1 hour (3600 seconds), Enterprise Custom. Pause/resume resets window; paused retention indefinite. Not a universal 86400-second lifetime cap.

idle_timeout_seconds.note: Fixed running TTL defaults to 5 minutes, not idle detection. Activity does not reset it; connect extends only, setTimeout resets. Timeout defaults to kill; pause/auto-resume opt-in. Auto-resume minimum TTL 5 minutes is not billing floor. No numeric idle-detector default established.

One-time $100 credit, not recurring or free ongoing compute; blocked on exhaustion until payment method added. No card to start. US default/all plans; EU/APAC require Pro and support.

Allocated RAM while running, including waiting. Pricing default 4 GiB conflicts with base/billing 512 MiB; build FAQ says custom rebuild without resources 1024 MiB. API memoryMB MiB minimum128 versus SDK comment MB and estimator label GB; retain units/scopes, inspect allocation, no universal default or conversion. Per-second meter, regional multipliers/floors unestablished.

10GiB Hobby/20+GiB Pro is free headroom above image contents per build-limitsFAQ, not maximum total template size or pooled allowance; EnterpriseCustom, higher via support/rebuild. Team-specific base-image cap separate. minFreeDiskMb MiB best-effort growth,0 no growth,never shrink.
